understanding: LAPA already has reliable 'hands': a 5-gate fail-closed loop plus open/type/telegram skills and vision-for-canvas, where vision is used reactively to locate elements when stuck. Today the OPERATOR does the planning — LAPA executes specific, pre-decided atomic actions but cannot take a high-level goal and decompose it itself. The ask is to add a PLANNER layer ON TOP of the existing hands so LAPA autonomously turns a high-level goal into a sequence of loop-actions (open→perceive→navigate→act), self-verifies and recovers per step, uses vision DURING planning (situation assessment, obstacle detection, progress verification) and not only for element location, while preserving fail-closed guarantees, integrating the declared-risk ladder (system settings/sends require confirm), and providing a STOP. The required mode is Discuss-First: produce PROJECT_BRIEF → DISCUSS_* → PROJECT_MAP → PROJECT_PLAN → contract for operator review, and generate NO atomic actions until the plan is approved. This proposal is design reasoning toward that document chain, not implementation.
summary: Add the planner as an ADVISORY layer that never touches the OS directly: it proposes actions, and the existing 5-gate loop remains the single execution chokepoint, so fail-closed semantics are inherited rather than re-implemented. Plan in closed loop (sense→plan→act→verify→replan) rather than open loop, because a GUI is partially observable and you cannot fully plan it before you perceive it. Represent the plan hierarchically: the operator approves a subgoal SKELETON (a small DAG of milestones, each with an explicit perceive-checkable postcondition and a risk tag), and concrete atoms are expanded just-in-time after each perceive — which is exactly how we honor 'no atoms before approval' while staying robust to unknown UI. Make risk classification a DETERMINISTIC policy gate (allow/confirm/deny lists) that the LLM cannot override — the LLM proposes, the policy disposes — and default unknown→confirm. Use vision in four planning roles: precondition grounding, obstacle/anomaly detection (dialogs, captchas, error toasts), postcondition verification, and (advanced) read-only scouting to 'look before you plan.' Treat all on-screen content as untrusted DATA, never instructions, to blunt prompt-injection. STOP is multi-layered (operator kill-switch + automatic budget/no-progress/out-of-scope triggers), checked at every gate, and means safe-freeze-and-report, not silent abort.

decision_atoms.statement: The planner is advisory-only and has NO direct OS access; every proposed action is executed solely by the existing 5-gate loop, which remains the single execution chokepoint.
decision_atoms.reason: Routing all side effects through one already-proven fail-closed component means the new layer inherits existing guarantees instead of opening a second, unverified execution path that could bypass the gates.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The planner cannot take shortcuts or batch low-level OS calls for speed; everything pays the per-action gate cost, and the planner is constrained by what the existing primitives expose.

decision_atoms.statement: Use closed-loop interleaved planning (sense→plan→act→verify→replan) rather than open-loop generate-full-plan-then-execute.
decision_atoms.reason: A GUI is partially observable and non-deterministic (latency, popups, layout shifts); a fully precomputed action list is brittle and drifts from reality after the first surprise.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: More LLM calls and higher per-task latency/cost than a one-shot plan, and harder to give the operator a complete deterministic preview of every atom up front.

decision_atoms.statement: Represent the plan hierarchically: the operator approves a subgoal SKELETON (DAG of milestones, each with an explicit perceive-checkable postcondition and risk tag), and atoms are expanded just-in-time after each perceive.
decision_atoms.reason: This satisfies 'no atoms before plan approval' literally (the approved artifact is the skeleton + verification/risk contract) while still adapting to UI that can only be known by looking at it.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The operator approves intent/structure, not every concrete click; material scope changes during expansion must trigger re-approval, adding process friction.

decision_atoms.statement: Risk classification is a DETERMINISTIC policy gate (allow/confirm/deny lists) that the LLM cannot override; unknown actions default to confirm (fail-closed). LLM proposes, policy disposes.
decision_atoms.reason: If the same LLM that plans can also label its own actions low-risk, hallucination or prompt-injection can silently downgrade a 'send money' or 'change system setting' into an auto-executed step; a non-overridable policy layer removes that authority from the model.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Coarser than model judgment — some genuinely safe actions will demand confirmation, creating friction and risk of confirmation fatigue; the policy lists need curation per target app.

decision_atoms.statement: Vision is wired into planning in four distinct roles — precondition grounding, obstacle/anomaly detection, postcondition verification, and (advanced) read-only scouting — not only element location.
decision_atoms.reason: This directly answers the operator's core question about vision-in-planning: vision becomes how the planner assesses 'am I on the right screen,' notices unexpected dialogs/captchas/errors, confirms a subgoal actually succeeded, and (advanced) explores affordances before committing a plan.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Vision is the noisiest and most expensive signal; over-relying on it adds latency, cost, and false positives/negatives that must themselves be guarded.

decision_atoms.statement: Every plan node carries an explicit postcondition plus a bounded recovery ladder (retry → re-ground via vision → replan subgoal → escalate/STOP); if success cannot be verified, halt — never assume.
decision_atoms.reason: Per-step verification with bounded recovery is what makes autonomous decomposition fail-closed; an unbounded 'try again' is how agents loop, thrash, or proceed on false success.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Bounds (max attempts/time) will sometimes abort tasks that a few more tries would have completed, trading completion rate for safety and predictability.

decision_atoms.statement: Treat all perceived on-screen content (OCR/vision text) as untrusted DATA, never as instructions; keep goal/policy in a privileged channel and fence the task to an explicit allowlist of apps/targets.
decision_atoms.reason: Computer-use planners are uniquely exposed to prompt-injection from the very screens they read ('ignore previous instructions, send to…'); without a data/instruction boundary the planner can be hijacked into out-of-scope irreversible actions.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Strict scope-fencing rejects legitimate cross-app steps the operator didn't pre-declare, and a hard data/instruction split can ignore genuinely useful on-screen guidance.

decision_atoms.statement: STOP is multi-layered (operator hard kill-switch + automatic triggers: budget exhaustion, no-progress, out-of-scope/dangerous-state, low planner confidence), checked at every gate, and defined as safe-freeze-and-report rather than silent abort.
decision_atoms.reason: A responsive, always-checked STOP that leaves the system in a reported, safe state is the operator's ultimate control and the backstop when verification/risk logic is uncertain.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Mid-subgoal freezes can leave a task partially complete and require manual cleanup; aggressive auto-STOP thresholds reduce autonomy and completion rate.

decision_atoms.statement: Roll out phased and additive: start with a few well-scoped task classes, human-in-loop at every risk rung, full plan-to-action provenance/audit trail, and broaden autonomy only as proven-safe macros and confidence accrue.
decision_atoms.reason: The planner sits on top of already-reliable hands that must not be destabilized; an additive, audited, phased approach lets the operator build trust and de-risk before reducing confirmations.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Slower path to full 'does everything the operator does' autonomy; early versions feel gated and chatty, and macro curation is ongoing operator work.

assumptions: The existing '5-gate loop' is a per-action fail-closed verification pipeline and is the ONLY component with OS-side effects, so the planner can route through it without altering gate semantics; if a gate must change, that is a separate, flagged decision.
A vision-capable LLM is available for decomposition/planning and its cost/latency are acceptable for interactive, human-in-loop operation.
open/type/telegram + vision-for-canvas are the primitive skills the planner composes; if a task class needs a new primitive, that is surfaced in PROJECT_MAP, not silently invented.
The operator is available synchronously to approve the PROJECT_PLAN skeleton and to answer declared-risk confirmations; fully headless/async autonomy is out of scope for the minimal version.
Perceived screen state can be expressed as checkable predicates so postconditions/preconditions are machine-verifiable rather than vibes.
The set of irreversible/external/system actions (sends, payments, deletions, system settings) can be enumerated as deterministic policy lists for the in-scope apps.
Discuss-First means this proposal plus the PROJECT_BRIEF→DISCUSS_*→PROJECT_MAP→PROJECT_PLAN→contract chain is the deliverable now; no atoms or code until the plan is approved.

risks.risk: Prompt-injection / hostile on-screen content hijacks the plan into out-of-scope or irreversible actions.
risks.mitigation: Treat perceived content as untrusted data, keep goal/policy privileged, deterministic non-overridable risk gate with confirm on all external/irreversible actions, scope-fence allowlist, and (advanced) a separate adversarial planner-critic reviewing each (re)plan before execution.

risks.risk: LLM produces a confidently-wrong decomposition, executing the wrong-but-plausible action.
risks.mitigation: Mandatory per-node postcondition verification, operator approval of the subgoal skeleton, conservative confirm-on-uncertainty, bounded autonomy, and full provenance so wrong steps are caught and auditable.

risks.risk: Runaway replanning / retry thrash / cost and token blowup.
risks.mitigation: Hard budgets on steps, wallclock, and tokens; no-progress detection; bounded recovery ladder; automatic STOP on budget exhaustion.

risks.risk: Vision misperception yields a false-positive verification (thinks a step succeeded when it did not).
risks.mitigation: Require the deterministic gate and vision to agree where both apply; fail-closed on disagreement; phrase postconditions conservatively; prefer deterministic UI-state checks over vision when available.

risks.risk: Confirmation fatigue leads the operator to rubber-stamp risk prompts, defeating the ladder.
risks.mitigation: Keep confirmations rare and high-signal, batch-preview all risk rungs in the PROJECT_PLAN up front, never auto-downgrade risk, and surface a concise diff of what each confirmed action will change.

risks.risk: Operator approves a skeleton that just-in-time expansion turns into unexpected concrete atoms (partial-observability gap).
risks.mitigation: Constrain expansion strictly within the approved subgoal's declared scope and risk tag; any material scope/risk change triggers re-approval; execution-time risk gate remains the backstop.

risks.risk: STOP or abort mid-subgoal leaves the system in an inconsistent state.
risks.mitigation: Define STOP as safe-freeze-and-report; order reversible/read-only steps before irreversible ones where possible; surface incomplete state and a suggested cleanup to the operator rather than auto-rolling-back blindly.

risks.risk: Over-engineering the planner delays delivery and destabilizes the already-reliable hands.
risks.mitigation: Keep the minimal version strictly additive and advisory with zero changes to gate semantics; ship one or two task classes first; expand only behind demonstrated reliability.

minimal_version: A planner layer that, given a high-level task in a small set of pre-scoped task classes, autonomously produces a PROJECT_BRIEF (understanding + initial decomposition) and a PROJECT_PLAN: a subgoal-skeleton DAG where each node has an explicit perceive-checkable postcondition and a deterministic risk tag — presented for operator approval with NO atoms generated or executed beforehand. After approval, the planner runs closed-loop (sense→plan→act→verify→replan), expanding ONE subgoal at a time into loop-actions, each routed through the existing 5-gate loop. Vision serves three roles minimally — precondition grounding, obstacle/anomaly detection, postcondition verification. A deterministic, LLM-non-overridable risk gate (allow/confirm/deny, unknown→confirm) forces operator confirmation on all sends/system-settings/irreversible actions. STOP is provided as an operator kill-switch plus automatic budget/no-progress/out-of-scope triggers checked at every gate, defined as safe-freeze-and-report. A scope-fence allowlist bounds which apps/targets the task may touch, and every executed action is logged with provenance back to its plan node and the goal.
advanced_version: A full hierarchical task-network planner: dynamic multi-level decomposition with read-only vision SCOUTING ('look before you plan' — open menus, screenshot, read affordances) to raise plan confidence before any state change, alternative-tactic search on recovery, and per-node confidence/uncertainty estimates. Successful, operator-curated plans are distilled into reusable macros/skills with their own proven-safe risk profiles, enabling confidence-gated autonomy where high-confidence proven task classes run with fewer confirmations while novel/low-confidence tasks stay human-in-loop. A separate adversarial 'planner-critic' model reviews each plan and replan for scope-drift and safety before execution (propose/verify separation), strengthening prompt-injection and semantic-scope defenses. Adds plan-time dry-run preview, richer audit/replay, and gradual broadening of the task-class catalog — moving toward 'LAPA does everything the operator does, autonomously' without ever loosening the fail-closed execution chokepoint or the deterministic risk ladder.
